result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers drop the 18% figure and the Hartwell Metals claim, give a short reason, and build the pitch on the contingency fee, the founders' carrier-billing background and a free invoice sample. A wins narrowly because its first follow-up adds real value (a list of the errors the founders saw from the carrier side) and it reminds them to add opt-out wording, though its first email offers two asks and its 'legal exposure' line leans slightly toward lecturing. B wins mainly on its first follow-up, which gives the reader a useful list of common billing errors instead of a thin nudge. It also adds a practical note about opt-out wording and contact details. A is slightly tighter and has a single clear ask, while B's first email offers either a call or an invoice sample.
